content.text:
I fixed the bug and checked it in the app. A brand-new data folder now shows "Drop a model or project to start", and the "could not be listed" line no longer appears in the log. I did this on the Windows machine, not your Mac. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Setup.** No other builds or JusPrin instances were running; the other Claude Code processes were idle. I pulled jusprin-newui (now at 516d057f1d). I reused the `peaceful-mayer-497851` worktree, which was clean and whose commit is saved on its own branch, on a new branch `claude/projects-folder-first-run`. I built in its tree, `C:\b\pmf`, with 4 parallel jobs.

**Cause.** Windows behaves the same way as you saw on the Mac. `is_directory()` on the missing `jusprin\projects` folder reports an error ("The system cannot find the path specified"), so the "no folder yet means no projects" shortcut never ran. The folder listing then failed and returned nothing, and Home showed the error and retried every second. Before the fix, the log had 22 of these lines in the first 25 seconds:
```
[error] Local projects could not be listed: C:\b\pff-dd-before\jusprin\projects: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

**The fix.** It's one word in fork code, in [ProjectAutosave.cpp:156](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:156):
```diff
-    if (!std::filesystem::is_directory(root, error) && !error)
+    // exists() clears the error for a path that is not there; is_directory()
+    // reports it as an error.
+    if (!std::filesystem::exists(root, error) && !error)
         return folders;
```
- **Why `exists()`:** the C++ standard requires it to clear the error when the path isn't there, and it keeps any other error, such as permission denied. Those errors still fall through to the folder listing, which fails, logs the error and returns nothing, as before.
- **Side effect:** it also fixes a second case. A file sitting where the projects folder belongs used to count as zero projects with no error; now it's reported as unreadable.
- **Both callers covered:** `projects()` and `projects_for_source()` both go through this function, and the new check tests both.

**The test.** I added `verify_projects_folder_before_first_save()` at the start of [real_adapter_harness.cpp](tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp:1424). Every harness run starts on a fresh temporary data folder with no projects folder yet, so this is the real first-run state.

| Check | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `first_run_has_no_projects_folder` | PASS | PASS |
| `first_run_lists_no_projects` | **FAIL** | PASS |
| `first_run_source_matches_no_projects` | **FAIL** | PASS |
| `projects_file_instead_of_folder_is_unreadable` | **FAIL** | PASS |

- **Two other failures:** the harness also fails `second_model_dropped` and `model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit`. I rebuilt it from clean jusprin-newui and those two fail there too, so they were already failing before my change.
- **Unreadable folder:** the case where you can't read the folder is still covered by the existing shell-harness check `verify_unavailable_projects_folder`. I didn't rerun that harness. Instead I ran the 42 `[home]` tests in `jusprin_tests`, including "projects that could not be listed reach the page as a problem", and they all pass.

**In the app.** I sent you three screenshots of these steps.
- **Before:** on an empty data folder, Home said "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying.", with the repeating log line above.
- **After:** on a new empty data folder, Home showed the first-run screen with "PROJECTS 0".
- **New project:** I clicked New, added the 20 mm test cube with Ctrl+I, and autosave created `jusprin\projects\p-19c2…`. Back on Home there was one card, "20mmbox-LF · Draft · Today". The listing error never appeared in that run's log.

**Other platforms.**
- **Windows:** tested. MSVC's `is_directory()` sets the error just as on your Mac, and `exists()` clears it.
- **macOS:** inferred, not tested. The C++ standard requires `exists()` to behave the same way there, so the fix should work.
- **Linux:** also inferred. I expect libstdc++'s `is_directory()` to report a missing folder as an error too, so Linux would have had the same bug, and `exists()` should fix it there as well.

Accept a hidden preset by name when the project uses it

A 3MF can select a system preset for a printer model the person never
enabled, so OrcaSlicer marks it hidden (is_visible false). JusPrin
refused such a preset by name wherever it checked is_visible, even
while the project was using it. In the 2026-10-28 walkthrough the
selected "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M" made settings_get fail with
unknown_preset, and the error suggested the same name it rejected.

The flag cannot answer "in use" by itself. OrcaSlicer's preset combo
box marks a selected hidden preset visible while it draws, but only
the stored preset: find_preset returns the edited copy for the
selected preset, and that copy keeps the flag it had when selected.

Printers::preset_by_name (new, header-only) accepts a preset that is
visible, selected in its collection, or in one of the project's
filament slots. Every lookup that refused hidden presets now uses it:
- the settings tools' target.preset (scope_preset)
- printer_setup and its preview: printer, process and filament names
- the header's Filament settings... and Printer settings... openers,
  which showed "The ... preset was not found"
- the printer chat's stock-profile lookup (stock_printer)
Hidden presets the project does not use are still refused. Pick
lists (presets_list, the filament chip's INSTALLED rows) keep
filtering on is_visible, which is what the flag is for.

Verified on c7e62ba4f8:
- Workspace adapter harness: 7 new checks. The three in-use checks
  failed before the change and pass after; the two hidden-unused
  rejections and two fixture checks pass both times. The other 14 failures (calibration
  flows, model drop) are the same before and after and also fail on
  the base branch.
- Shell harness --printer-menu: 3 new checks (both header openers and
  stock_printer) failed before, pass after; 0 failures. --printer-setup,
  --mcp and --task-chat pass.
- Real app with the walkthrough 3MF, through MCP: settings_get and
  printer_setup_preview accept the selected hidden A1M filament and
  still refuse an unused hidden one.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M62CNK7GRF4WHGCXGYYF51TN

input.content:
Show the first-run screen when no projects folder exists yet

The projects folder is made by the first saved version, so a new data
folder has none. project_folders() tested for it with
is_directory(root, error) and returned an empty list only when that
left the error clear. libc++ (macOS) and MSVC (Windows) both report a
missing path as an error there, so the listing went on, failed, and
returned nothing: Home said "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin
will keep trying." and logged "Local projects could not be listed"
once a second, instead of showing "Drop a model or project to start".

exists(root, error) clears the error for a missing path, as the
standard requires, and keeps every other error (permission denied, I/O
failure), which still reaches the listing and is still logged and
reported. A file where the folder belongs, which is_directory() also
let through as no projects, now fails the listing and is reported.
Both callers, projects() and projects_for_source(), go through this.

- Workspace adapter harness: 5 new checks at the start of the run,
  on its fresh data folder. The two missing-folder listings and the
  file-instead-of-folder check failed before the change and pass
  after. The other 2 failures (second_model_dropped,
  model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit) also fail on the base branch.
- jusprin_tests [home]: 42 test cases pass.
- Real app on an empty --datadir: before, the error screen and the
  repeating log line; after, the first-run screen and no such line.
  New, then importing a cube, then back to Home lists the project.
